advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Seed `"indeterminate": []` in `_empty_binding_drift()` so the JSON bucket is always present like its siblings.
evidence: bridge_fsck.py:349 `drift.setdefault("indeterminate", []).append(...)` — created only when a terminal key-set cell is hit
bridge_fsck.py:591 JSON envelope dumps `binding_drift` dict directly, so the key is absent from output when empty
test asserts the asymmetry: `assert "indeterminate" not in live` / `assert "indeterminate" not in done` in test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py
schema bridge_fsck.schema.json:23 catalogs `indeterminate` as a peer array bucket alongside always-present buckets
advisory.finding: The `indeterminate` drift bucket is not seeded in `_empty_binding_drift()`, so it is created lazily via `setdefault` only when non-empty. It is therefore conditionally present in the emitted JSON `binding_drift` envelope, whereas every sibling bucket (would_terminal, local_gone, retired_overlap, dangling, absent_in_window_unprobed, unbound_jira) is always present as `[]`. This asymmetry means a consumer indexing `binding_drift["indeterminate"]` KeyErrors on clean/full-payload snapshots.
scenarios: A downstream JSON consumer reads binding_drift['indeterminate'] on any full-payload or clean snapshot and hits a KeyError instead of an empty list.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `"indeterminate": []` to the dict returned by `_empty_binding_drift()` and replace `drift.setdefault("indeterminate", []).append(...)` with `drift["indeterminate"].append(...)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider fencing terminal-local cells on absence of a resolvable Jira status (e.g. `_jira_status(jira_fields) == ""`) rather than the exact `jira_fields == {}` shape.
evidence: bridge_fsck.py:348 `if classify_mod.local_state(local) is LocalState.TERMINAL and jira_fields == {}:` — exact-equality guard
classify.py:282-283 `_jira_status` returns '' when fields is falsy/missing, which is not a terminal status → TERMINAL_TRANSITION at classify.py:244
ABSENCE: no branch handles a present key whose value is None or a status-less non-empty dict
advisory.finding: The terminal-local fence keys strictly on `jira_fields == {}`. A key-set/degraded snapshot entry whose value is `None` or a non-empty dict lacking a `status` field bypasses the fence and reaches the classifier, where `_jira_status` returns '' and yields a false `would_terminal` (TERMINAL_TRANSITION). Only the exact `{}` form is fenced.
scenarios: A snapshot narrowing scheme that stores present keys as null or a partial dict without status would resurrect the exact false-terminal-drift regression this change fences against.

evidence: src/rebar/schemas/bridge_fsck.schema.json:23: the `description` is a JSON Schema annotation (draft 2020-12) — annotations do not affect validation, so no non-human consumer reads this exact wording; only prose.
The adjacent `assert indeterminate["type"] == "array"` (line 247) is a valid structural-contract assertion; the description-substring assertion is the change-detector portion.
advisory.finding: test_bridge_fsck_schema_catalogs_indeterminate_drift asserts a prose substring of the JSON Schema `description` annotation ('informational; never alerts'), which is human-facing text no validator/parser branches on — a behavior-preserving reword of the description would break the test without any observable-behavior change (change-detector).
scenarios: Someone rewords the schema `description` (e.g. 'informational; does not alert') without changing the never-alerts behavior — the test fails spuriously.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove the `assert "informational; never alerts" in indeterminate["description"]` line, relying on the CLI exit-code=0 assertion in test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev_heldout.py to prove the never-alerts behavior.
